content: The pharmacodynamic interaction between vadadustat and ethinylestradiol may lead to an increase in the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol. This necessitates careful monitoring and caution during co-administration. Vadadustat may also increase the exposure of substrates of the Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP). It is essential to monitor for adverse effects related to BCRP substrates and adjust their doses according to their product labeling. Both ethinylestradiol and valoctocogene roxaparvovec can increase their effects through unspecified mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Medications with potential hepatotoxicity, when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec, may elevate the risk of increased liver enzyme levels. Close monitoring and consideration of alternative medications are recommended to mitigate potential drug interactions. Ethinylestradiol can decrease the levels or effects of valproic acid by enhancing its elimination, potentially leading to increased seizure frequency. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both valsartan and drospirenone can elevate serum potassium levels, necessitating therapy adjustments and close monitoring. Similarly, voclosporin and drospirenone can increase serum potassium levels, requiring caution and monitoring. Voriconazole can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone can enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism, requiring caution and monitoring. Drospirenone also increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib, abiraterone, acalabrutinib, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown but warrants caution. Acetazolamide can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Agrimony may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of alfentanil, alfuzosin, alpelisib, alprazolam, ambrisentan, amiodarone, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are of minor significance but should still be monitored. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of amitriptyline and amoxapine through unspecified mechanisms, potentially altering the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and increasing their plasma concentrations and adverse effects. Anastrozole can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinylestradiol can also increase the levels or effects of antipyrine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of apalutamide, apixaban, apomorphine, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Aspirin may decrease the levels or effects of drospirenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of astemizole, atazanavir, atogepant, atorvastatin, avanafil, avapritinib, avatrombopag, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. When treating immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), co-administration of avatrombopag with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors requires a reduced starting dose of avatrombopag. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of axitinib, bedaquiline, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, benzphetamine, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Birch and brimonidine may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of bortezomib, bosentan, bosutinib, brentuximab vedotin, brexpiprazole, brigatinib, bromocriptine, budesonide, buprenorphine, buspirone, busulfan, cabozantinib, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cadexomer iodine may decrease renal clearance of drospirenone, potentially leading to hyperkalemia. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of calcifediol, calcitriol, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It may decrease the levels of calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate by increasing renal clearance. Drospirenone can also increase the levels or effects of capmatinib, carbamazepine, cariprazine, chlordiazepoxide, chloroquine, chlorpheniramine, ciclesonide inhaled, cilostazol, cisapride, citalopram, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of clarithromycin, clomipramine, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 or CYP1A2 metabolism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of clarithromycin, clonazepam, clorazepate, cobicistat, cobimetinib, cocaine topical, colchicine, conivaptan, conjugated estrogens, copanlisib, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Corn silk may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. Cyclophosphamide can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone can increase the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, dabrafenib, and other drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism.
